title: Cellular and circuit mechanisms of the therapeutic action of inhaled nitrous oxide in rodent models of chronic stress
text:
A single dose of the dissociative anesthetic nitrous oxide produces rapid and durable improvements in
depressive symptoms that persist in otherwise treatment-resistant patients. The driving hypothesis of this
proposal is that nitrous oxide induces distinct changes in neuronal activity on the time scale of minutes during
administration, and engages neuroplastic mechanisms, over hours to days, that are mechanistically linked to
long-lasting therapeutic effects. This project will use in vivo imaging techniques to investigate the action of nitrous
oxide at the level of neurons and their neuronal connections over the natural trajectory of treatment and post-
treatment in individual animals to better define the novel forms of neuroplasticity underlie the long-standing
therapeutic effects.

title: Innovative Therapy to Treat Women with Angina with Nonobstructive CAD (ANOCA) and Coronary Microvascular Disease
text:
Since there is a lack of evidence for treatment in this population, this proposal will fill an unmet need in
managing women with angina with nonobstructive coronary artery disease (ANOCA) and microvascular
disease. Our proposal will significantly advance our understanding of SGLT2 inhibitors' potential benefits in
coronary microvascular disease. Knowing SGLT2i's effect on inflammation pathways and markers of systemic
Inflammation will allow for the discovery of a potential mechanism of SGLT2i's cardioprotective effects and
allow us to design more targeted studies, such as those that assess the drug's impact on specific cytokines.

title: Investigating T cell Circuits in the Lymphatic System During Melanoma Progression
text:
Lymph nodes are hubs for anti-tumor immune surveillance, but their immune potential can be disrupted by tumor
invasion and regional metastasis. We investigate a lymphatic circuit that maintains robust anti-tumor immunity
in the tumor-draining lymph node, tracking the developmental fate of egressing cytotoxic T cells and tumor-
associated antigens as a function of metastasis. We propose that our studies will identify clinically relevant
strategies to stratify risk for recurrence and future strategies for immunotherapeutic reinvigoration.

title: Development of an Ultra-Broadband Microscope
text: This project aims to develop an innovative ultra-broadband microscope that eliminates chromatic aberration and extends high-resolution imaging capabilities across a broad spectral range from ultraviolet (UV) to infrared (IR). By integrating advanced freeform optics and precision fabrication techniques, this microscope will overcome the limitations of conventional refractive and reflective systems, providing superior imaging performance for biomedical biological sciences research. The proposed technology will enable high-contrast, multimodal imaging with unprecedented spectral coverage, advancing biological research and biomedical imaging to drive new scientific discoveries and enhance the understanding of complex biological processes.

title: Investigations of Lyme spirochete transmission as a complex network of microbial and ecological interactions
text: The study of Bb transmission dynamics has been foundational for understanding the emergence of LD and other tick-borne diseases. This work will comprehensively expand this foundation by incorporating myriad effects of the tick microbiome to improve understanding of the Bb enzootic transmission cycle, which, in turn, directly informs LD risk. The conceptual and quantitative frameworks developed will be foundational for microbiome-informed vector-borne disease modeling in the future.

title: Measuring and Predicting Appropriate Antibiotic Use to Combat Resistant Bacteria
text:
Antibiotic resistant bacteria already cause over 2.8 million illnesses and 35,000 deaths every year, with
antibiotic misuse incurring up to $42 billion in avoidable costs per year in the US alone. Urinary tract infections
(UTIs) in particular are the most common human bacterial infection accounting for 25-50% of antibiotic
prescriptions with resistance rates among causative bacteria now exceeding 20% for commonly used
antibiotics. The most important action to slow the spread of these resistant infections is improving antibiotic
prescribing and stewardship, which this project seeks to improve through novel machine learning and data-
driven methods to measure and predict effective antibiotic choices for urinary tract infections.

title: Growth plate cartilage stem cells for skeletal repair after injury
text:
In this project, the investigators study the role of growth plate stem cells in hopes of gaining insights in the
skeletal repair process after physeal injury. The results of the study will help bioengineering efforts directed
towards growth plate cartilage regeneration.

title: Signaling, Genomes, and Networks
text: SIGNALING, GENOMES, AND NETWORKS (SGN) The Cancer Signaling, Genomes, and Networks (SGN) Program brings together basic, translational, and clinical investigators who are aligned with one or more scientific research themes based on their focus areas: 1) Cancer Cell Biology and Biochemistry; 2) Cancer Genomics and Computational Oncology; and 3) Translational Oncology. Research in SGN is focused on discovering mechanisms underlying the initiation, progression, and metastasis of cancer types relevant to patients in our catchment area and nationally. SGN laboratory scientists identify pathways, molecular targets, and mechanisms of action of anti-cancer treatments, and develop innovative genetic, molecular, and computational approaches to cancer research to maximize benefits to human health, in concert with SGN clinical investigators who translate these discoveries into new treatment strategies and cutting-edge clinical trials. DCC Shared Resources provide enabling access to technologies that are essential to the success of the Program. SGN is led by Arminja Kettenbach PhD, and Konstantin Dragnev MD, who direct the basic science and clinical research aspects of the program, respectively. Our 57 members represent 11 departments across the Dartmouth Geisel School of Medicine, Dartmouth College of Arts and Sciences, and Dartmouth Health. Among the Members of the SGN Program, 36 are laboratory-based scientists, 19 are clinicians, and 2 are clinician-scientists. Current peer-reviewed cancer-relevant funding totals $9.0M (29% increase compared to 2019), of which $2.3M (26%) is from NCI (28% increase compared to 2019). As of 7/31/2023, SGN Members have authored 379 publications in the current award period, of which 24% are high impact. Collaborative publications include 17% intra-programmatic, 28% inter-programmatic, and 28% inter-NCI- cancer center manuscripts. SGN research resulted in new intellectual property and two new companies. SGN- led clinical research resulted in 110 investigator-initiated treatment studies enrolling 350 patients (46% of all DCC accruals), and 115 interventional trials enrolling 416 patients (6% of all DCC accruals). This activity represents an over 3-fold increase in accruals to both interventional and treatment studies from the prior funding cycle. Moving forward, the SGN Program will continue to strengthen multidisciplinary collaborations between basic, translational, and clinical researchers, prioritize mentoring junior faculty members to achieve academic independence, train junior scientists in basic, translational and clinical cancer research, and promote the partnerships of clinicians and laboratory scientists to drive the development of investigator-initiated clinical studies that reflect areas of priority identified by our community partners.

title: Precision imaging for risk stratification and personalized therapy of oropharyngeal cancer
text:
The incidence of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancer has been rapidly increasing in the US. In this
project, we propose to develop and validate quantitative imaging biomarkers to predict risks of
locoregional relapse and distant metastasis in oropharyngeal cancer. This has the potential to
optimize selection of patients who are eligible for treatment de-escalation in HPV-positive disease,
paving the way for precision medicine in oropharyngeal cancer.

title: Structural and functional basis of 5-HT3R modulation by antidepressants
text:
Serotonin Type 3 Receptor (5-HT3R) pathophysiology is associated with major depressive disorder and
many antidepressants interact with 5-HT3Rs through unknown mechanisms. This study seeks to investigate the
precise molecular interactions through which antidepressants modulate 5-HT3Rs. The findings from this work
may lead to the development of novel, safe, and effective small molecules targeting 5-HT3Rs.
Specific Aims

title: A pilot study of cross-cutting e-health prevention approaches to address campus sexual assault and alcohol misuse
text:
Sexual violence (SV) and alcohol misuse are critical and interconnected problems among
college students. Yet, despite the proliferation of evidence-based sexual violence and alcohol
misuse programs for colleges, there has been no effort to integrate these programs to provide a
comprehensive approach to reducing SV and alcohol misuse, therefore it is crucial to implement
and evaluate comprehensive prevention programs that address this significant public health
problem impacting young adults ages 18-24. The proposed R15 AREA research study fills a
major gap in SV and alcohol misuse prevention on college campuses by implementing and
testing the feasibility of a multi-level social ecological model (e.g., individual, relationship,
community) approach consisting of six established e-health primary prevention strategies in a
three-phase study that includes formative evaluation (N=870), a feasibility study (N=350) and
implementation science interviews (N=15 participants from the Student Advisory Board and
N=15 campus stakeholders).

title: Identification of Genetic Variants that Influence Compulsive Alcohol Intake in Outbred Rats
text:
This is a multidisciplinary, highly collaborative proposal that combines next-generation sequencing with state-
of-the-art behavioral screening in a unique, genetically diverse, nonhuman animal model. The goals of this
proposal are to identify gene variants that are associated with compulsive alcohol use, alcohol tolerance and
response to FDA approved medications using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in behaviorally
characterized heterogeneous stock rats, and to establish a data/tissue repository accessible to all researchers
to study the cellular and molecular mechanisms of alcohol addiction. Results from these studies have the
potential to have a sustained and powerful impact on the field of addiction because they will identify novel
druggable targets, provide a comprehensive analysis of compulsive alcohol use in males and females, and
create a unique data/tissue repository that will facilitate follow-up and replication studies.

title: Translational Nonhuman Primate Regenerative Medicine and Gene Therapy/Genome Editing Resource Program
text:
There is a critical need for investigators to have access to a dedicated resource for evaluating new
regenerative medicine and gene therapy/somatic cell genome editing approaches with nonhuman primates for
the treatment of human diseases. The overarching goals of this application are to provide models, tools, and
technologies to address safe and effective treatments across age groups, and ensure opportunities are
available to obtain preclinical data that will lead to human clinical trials.

title: Development and Application of PET-enabled Dual-Energy CT Imaging
text:
Public Health Relevance Statement: Molecular imaging with PET/CT has been widely used in oncology
but current methods have limited ability to characterize tissue compositions quantitatively. This project
develops and translates a PET-enabled dual-energy CT method to offer quantitative material
decomposition on PET/CT scanners. The enabled ability will open new avenues to improve molecular
imaging and would make a significant impact in numerous clinical applications where the
characterization of tissue composition matters, such as for bone-marrow PET/CT imaging or contrast-
enhanced PET/CT imaging.

title: Fibro/Adipogenic Progenitor Metabolic Reprogramming for Age-Related Muscle Fibrosis
text:
Maintaining muscular strength into old age is essential for independence, safety and daily activities; therefore,
understanding contributors which lead to the progression of muscle fibrosis in aging will provide novel therapeutic
strategies to delay or prevent sarcopenia. I have identified fibro/adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) as novel
contributors to aged muscle fibrosis but the cellular and molecular events that lead to this are unclear. The goal
of this proposal is to investigate FAPs through sarcopenia development to elucidate therapeutic approaches
which leverage FAP metabolism to delay or prevent fibrosis and weakness associated with sarcopenia.

title: The mechanism of extra-visual circadian photoentrainment in mammals
text:
The surface of the mammalian body is directly exposed to environmental solar light. We
have found that many circadian clocks within these tissues respond directly to short-
wavelength light using opsin photoreceptors. The goal of this proposal is to analyze the
mechanisms of this local photoreception in the mammalian circadian system.

title: Mechanisms of Photoreceptor Contribution to Retinal Inflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy
text:
Diabetic retinopathy blinds approximately 12% of diabetic patients each year and its incidence is expected to
increase. While there are currently no therapeutic strategies directed at its early stages, there is accumulating
evidence that retinal photoreceptors are involved in the pathogenesis of diabetic retinopathy and are major
contributors to diabetes-induced local inflammation in the retina. This project aims to study the responses of
photoreceptors to hyperglycemia and interventions that address this pathway with the potential to be effective
in the early stages of diabetic retinopathy to prevent the development of vision-threatening pathology.

title: Functional characterization of the lineage plasticity landscape of cholangiocarcinoma
text:
This R01 proposal focuses on the innovative concept of lineage plasticity to advance our understanding
of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), a challenging cancer with limited treatment options and poor prognoses.
By delineating the dynamic transitions in CCA lineage states and their impact on tumor initiation,
growth, and drug resistance, this study aims to redefine therapeutic approaches. Employing cutting-
edge methodologies including spatial epigenomics and plasmid mix-and-match mouse models, the
project is poised to create a paradigm shift in how CCA is molecularly analyzed and treated.

title: Physical Activity Measurement in Toddlers
text:
Physical activity has numerous health benefits. Physical activity behaviors develop from very early childhood.
This proposed project aims to develop an analytic tool to recognize the activity types of toddlers, such as
walking/running, standing, sitting, and being carried by an adult. The analytic tool developed will be useful to
accurately evaluate physical activity levels among toddlers.

title: Testing the effects of tirzepatide on colorectal cancer incidence and outcomes in a mouse model
text:
This project seeks to understand the potential influence of the incretin mimetic, tirzepatide on colorectal cancer
incidence and outcomes using a genetically engineered mouse model. The model will be used to evaluate the
potential for differences in outcome based on whether tirzepatide is started before cancer (prevention setting),
or after a cancer has started (outcomes). Given the increased use of incretin medications, it is imperative to
understand the potential influence of these agents on colorectal cancer.
